trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full read of alg:wedderburn-decomposition. No constructions from the ten categories. VERIFIED: the Frame-Robinson-Thrall formula d_lambda = n!/prod_c h_lambda(c) is stated correctly; 'at most 30 partitions' for n <= 9 is exactly p(9) = 30; and correctness condition 4's Lean citation checks out - QOU.Mathlib.numStandardYoungTableaux_mul_hookLengthProduct in HookLengthFormula.lean carries a real proof term with no sorry (the three 'sorry' grep hits in that file are the words 'sorry-free' in docstrings).
trap-negation-contrast.notes: NOT A TRAP, reported separately, two items. (1) Algorithm step 2a and correctness condition 4 contradict each other inside this one block. Step 2a says to compute d_lambda by the hook-length formula at q = 1 and 'then q-deform via [hook]_q'; condition 4 says the block dimensions are 'exact integers'. Condition 4 is the correct one - by the Tits deformation argument H_n(q) is isomorphic to the group algebra for generic q, so the Wedderburn block dimensions are the undeformed integers; the q-deformed hook product is the quantum dimension, a different quantity. (2) The Notes call Wedderburn 'the most expensive step in the chain for n > 6', while alg:markov-trace states 'the dominant cost is the GS reduction in step 1'. Both are in this appendix; at most one is right.
